commits.message:
cellLen measures each cluster as Rich's cell_len does, from Rich's own width table (rich-unfiled-791c.s186) (#455)

* cellLen counts Spacing_Marks, jamo, Prepend letters, conjuncts and the soft hyphen as Rich's cell_len does (rich-unfiled-791c.s186)

* cellLen measures each cluster as Rich's cell_len does, from Rich's own width table (rich-unfiled-791c.s186)

The exception list over string-width broke what it did not list: measuring a
listed code point as NUL re-segments its neighbours, so a virama+ZWJ
half-form gained a cell Rich does not give it. string-width sizes a cluster
by its first code point; Rich sums a width per code point. No list of
exceptions closes that gap, so cellLen now runs Rich's algorithm over each
grapheme cluster:
each code point's cells from Rich 15's Unicode 17 table, a ZWJ taking the code
point after it into its glyph, and VS16 widening the code point before it.

src/core/cell-widths.ts is that table, generated by scripts/cell-widths.py.
Being vendored, it gives the same width on every Node, whatever that Node's
ICU says. Measuring per cluster keeps cellLen additive over the cuts every
other cells function makes. The one cost is that a ZWJ or VS16 can no longer
reach into the next cluster the way Rich's can; tests pin that.

string-width was the only runtime dependency and is gone. No installed package
holds up engines.node any more, so >=20 is src/'s own claim, which
.github/actions/node-floor/ checks on Node 20.
